rule_message: Affected versions of mlflow are vulnerable to Origin Validation Error. Lack of Origin header validation in MLflow's REST server enables DNS rebinding attacks that bypass the browser's same-origin policy. A malicious webpage can then issue unauthorized experiment-management calls (e.g. list, update or delete experiments), leading to data exfiltration, tampering or destruction.

rule_message: Affected versions of storybook are vulnerable to Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor / Inclusion of Sensitive Information in an Include File / Insertion of Sensitive Information into Externally-Accessible File or Directory. A bug in Storybook's build process causes any environment variables defined in a `.env` file (e.g. `.env.local`) in the project directory to be unexpectedly bundled into the static output. When that build is published to the web, those variables —including any secrets—are exposed in the client‐side source.

rule_message: Affected versions of open-webui are vulnerable to Improper Encoding or Escaping of Output / Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'). A stored XSS in Open-WebUI's Notes PDF download: in `src/lib/components/notes/utils.ts`, the `downloadPdf()` function directly assigns `note.data.content.html` to `innerHTML` without sanitization, allowing an attacker to import a Markdown file containing malicious SVG (e.g. `<svg onload="…">`) that executes arbitrary JavaScript when a user downloads the note as PDF—enabling session token theft.

rule_message: Affected versions of ray are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) / Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection'). Ray's dashboard exposes unauthenticated critical endpoints (`/api/jobs`, `/api/job_agent/jobs/`) that are "protected" only by a heuristic blocking browser requests based on `User-Agent` starting with "Mozilla." Firefox and Safari's fetch API can override this header, so an attacker who lures a developer into visiting a malicious page and performs a DNS rebinding attack can bypass the check, POST to those endpoints, and execute arbitrary shell commands on the developer's machine.

rule_message: Affected versions of github.com/opencontainers/runc are vulnerable to Race Condition Enabling Link Following / UNIX Symbolic Link (Symlink) Following. A flaw in runc's `maskedPaths` handling lets unprivileged container processes hijack or remove the container's `/dev/null` before it's bind-mounted as a "mask" source. Because runc never verifies the inode is a real `/dev/null`, an attacker can replace it with a symlink or alternate file and force runc to mount arbitrary host paths into the container. This can be abused for host denial-of-service (e.g. mounting a writable `/proc/sysrq-trigger`), container escape to root (by remounting and abusing `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern`), or host information disclosure. In addition, runc silently ignores `ENOENT` on the bind-mount source, allowing attackers to bypass all `maskedPaths` protections and gain read access to normally hidden host procfs entries.

rule_message: Affected versions of github.com/opencontainers/runc and github.com/opencontainers/selinux are vulnerable to Race Condition Enabling Link Following / UNIX Symbolic Link (Symlink) Following. An attacker who can race runc with a sibling container sharing mounts can exploit a logic flaw that misdirects writes to `/proc`—including LSM label files under `/proc/self/attr/…` and sysctls under `/proc/sys/…`—via symlinks or bind‐mounts, bypassing LSM label enforcement and enabling arbitrary procfs writes (for example to `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` or `/proc/sysrq-trigger`), leading to host denial-of-service or privilege escalation.

rule_message: Affected versions of github.com/containerd/containerd and github.com/containerd/containerd/v2 are vulnerable to Incorrect Execution-Assigned Permissions. Containerd by default creates several of its data directories (e.g. /var/lib/containerd with 0o711, and /run/containerd/io.containerd.grpc.v1.cri or …sandbox.controller.v1.shim with 0o755/0o711) with permissions more permissive than 0o700, allowing any local user on the host to read its metadata store, content store or Kubernetes volume contents (which may include setuid binaries), leading to information disclosure or local privilege escalation.

rule_message: Affected versions of aim are vulnerable to Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF). The tracking server in Aim uses an overly permissive CORS policy that accepts requests from any origin, enabling CSRF attacks on all endpoints. An attacker can exploit this to perform unauthorized actions and chain it with other flaws—such as remote code execution, denial of service, or arbitrary file read/write— against the self-hosted experiment tracking service.

rule_message: Affected versions of aim are vulnerable to Synchronous Access of Remote Resource without Timeout / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. The HTTP client used by the Aim tracking server (in methods like `_run_read_instructions` and related calls) does not enforce timeouts on external resource requests. A slow or unresponsive remote endpoint can hang the tracking server indefinitely, causing a denial of service by blocking all incoming requests.

A maliciously crafted pattern can match and delete arbitrary files on the host, leading to data loss or system compromise.

rule_message: Affected versions of axios are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). Axios can be tricked into sending requests to arbitrary domains when provided with an absolute URL—even if a baseURL is configured—resulting in a potential SSRF and credential leakage vulnerability. If an attacker can control the URL input, they might cause sensitive headers (such as API keys) to be sent to an unintended destination or gain access to internal network resources. Note that unsanitized input should NEVER be sent to any axios function, as they all pose a risk of SSRF.

rule_message: Affected versions of pillow are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read. The PCX decoder in Pillow (PcxDecode) can perform a buffer over-read when handling a crafted PCX file because it trusts a user-supplied stride value for its buffer calculations. An attacker supplying a malicious PCX image can trigger out-of-bounds reads, potentially leading to application crashes or disclosure of memory contents.

rule_message: Affected versions of litellm are vulnerable to Improper Authorization / Incorrect Privilege Assignment. When a user with the role `internal_user_viewer` logs into the application, they are provided with an overly privileged API key. This key can be used to access all the admin functionality of the application including endpoints such as `/users/list` and `/users/get_users`. This vulnerability allows for privilege escalation within the application, enabling any account to become a PROXY ADMIN.

rule_message: Affected versions of gradio are vulnerable to Improper Limitation Of A Pathname To A Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'). The vulnerability arises from its utilization of two APIs, `/queue/join` and `/queue/data`, for data interchange between the frontend and backend, wherein inadequate data management permits attackers to manipulate the payload sent to `/queue/data`, resulting in the execution of unauthorized actions; attackers exploit this vulnerability by altering the `path` parameter in requests to `/queue/data`, inducing the backend to duplicate a specified file to a cache directory , subsequently enabling attackers to directly download the file via the /file=temp_path_to_the_copied_file API endpoint, thereby gaining unauthorized access to sensitive files.

rule_message: tensorflow-gpu versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3, tensorflow-cpu versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3, and tensorflow versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3 are vulnerable to Null Pointer Dereference / Access Of Uninitialized Pointer. rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions / Reachable Assertion. A denial-of-service crash can occur during shape inference when TensorFlow attempts to specialize an op's full_type attributes. In InferenceContext::PreInputInit it uses DCHECK to verify that full_type::SpecializeType succeeded, then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the result. Because DCHECK is a no-op in release builds, a malformed or malicious op definition whose type specialization fails will hit ValueOrDie() on an error status, crashing the process.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere / Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition. In several TensorFlow utility and library routines, Python's insecure tempfile.mktemp is used to generate temporary file (and even directory) names without atomic creation. This TOC/TOU race allows a local attacker or malicious process to pre-create or hijack the path before TensorFlow uses it, potentially leading to unintended file overwrite, data injection, or code execution.

The excessive CPU time and RAM required can hinder worker processes, leading to exhaustion or termination with many concurrent requests.

rule_message: Affected versions of gunicorn are vulnerable to Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'). Gunicorn fails to properly validate the HTTP Transfer-Encoding header, defaulting to content-length processing. This behavior enables TE.CL request smuggling, which attackers can exploit to trigger cache poisoning, data exposure, session manipulation, SSRF, XSS, and DoS attacks.

rule_message: Affected versions of gradio are vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (Ssrf). rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Recursion / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. A typo in TensorFlow's SpecializeType implementation causes the inner loop to call `mutable_args(i)` instead of `mutable_args(j)`, allowing heap out-of-bounds read/write of full_type arguments. An attacker who supplies a maliciously crafted model or graph with specially crafted operator full types can trigger heap corruption when the model is loaded, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or denial of service.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to  Integer Overflow or Wraparound. An integer overflow in TensorFlow's grappler cost estimator can be triggered by a maliciously crafted graph with extremely large tensor dimensions. In `OpLevelCostEstimator::CalculateTensorSize`, the product of the element count and element size (`count * size`) isn't checked for overflow, so it can wrap around and yield a much smaller (or negative) tensor size. Downstream code that allocates or indexes based on this miscomputed size may then under-allocate buffers or perform out-of-bounds accesses, leading to memory corruption.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Integer Overflow or Wraparound. It is recommended to use the downstream TensorFlow Decision Forests project, instead of the unmaintained boosted trees implementation.

rule_message: Affected versions of gradio are vulnerable to Improper Limitation Of A Pathname To A Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal'). The vulnerability arises from its utilization of two APIs, `/queue/join` and `/queue/data`, for data interchange between the frontend and backend, wherein inadequate data management permits attackers to manipulate the payload sent to `/queue/data`, resulting in the execution of unauthorized actions; attackers exploit this vulnerability by altering the `path` parameter in requests to `/queue/data`, inducing the backend to duplicate a specified file to a cache directory , subsequently enabling attackers to directly download the file via the /file=temp_path_to_the_copied_file API endpoint, thereby gaining unauthorized access to sensitive files.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions / Reachable Assertion. A denial-of-service crash can occur during shape inference when TensorFlow attempts to specialize an op's full_type attributes. In InferenceContext::PreInputInit it uses DCHECK to verify that full_type::SpecializeType succeeded, then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the result. Because DCHECK is a no-op in release builds, a malformed or malicious op definition whose type specialization fails will hit ValueOrDie() on an error status, crashing the process.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere / Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition. In several TensorFlow utility and library routines, Python's insecure tempfile.mktemp is used to generate temporary file (and even directory) names without atomic creation. This TOC/TOU race allows a local attacker or malicious process to pre-create or hijack the path before TensorFlow uses it, potentially leading to unintended file overwrite, data injection, or code execution.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to  Integer Overflow or Wraparound. An integer overflow in TensorFlow's grappler cost estimator can be triggered by a maliciously crafted graph with extremely large tensor dimensions. In `OpLevelCostEstimator::CalculateTensorSize`, the product of the element count and element size (`count * size`) isn't checked for overflow, so it can wrap around and yield a much smaller (or negative) tensor size. Downstream code that allocates or indexes based on this miscomputed size may then under-allocate buffers or perform out-of-bounds accesses, leading to memory corruption.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions / Reachable Assertion. A denial-of-service crash can occur during shape inference when TensorFlow attempts to specialize an op's full_type attributes. In InferenceContext::PreInputInit it uses DCHECK to verify that full_type::SpecializeType succeeded, then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the result. Because DCHECK is a no-op in release builds, a malformed or malicious op definition whose type specialization fails will hit ValueOrDie() on an error status, crashing the process.

rule_message: Affected versions of pillow are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read. An attacker supplying a malicious PCX image can trigger out-of-bounds reads, potentially leading to application crashes or disclosure of memory contents.

rule_message: Affected versions of h2o are vulnerable to External Control Of File Name Or Path / Externally Controlled Reference To A Resource In Another Sphere. The vulnerability lies in the unrestricted location capabilities of the `Export` function in Frames, enabling the complete overwrite of local server files, potentially causing a remote server denial of service by manipulating system files or embedding backdoors, despite limited control over output formats like CSV/XLS/etc, as certain configuration files and services might interpret the h2o CSV format and allow arbitrary exploitation.

rule_message: Affected versions of h2o are vulnerable to Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. The `run_tool` command in the `rapids` component allows the `main` function of any class under the `water.tools` namespace to be called. One such class, `MojoConvertTool`, crashes the server when invoked with an invalid argument, causing a denial of service.

rule_message: Affected versions of h2o are vulnerable to Synchronous Access of Remote Resource without Timeout. The typeahead endpoint in H2O performs a HEAD request to verify resource existence without setting a timeout. This allows an attacker to force the application to hang by pointing the request to an attacker-controlled server that never responds, leading to a denial-of-service condition.

rule_message: Affected versions of h2o are vulnerable to External Control of File Name or Path. The /99/Models/{name}/json endpoint in H2O can be exploited because it directly uses the user-controlled mexport.dir parameter to specify the file path for writing model details. This allows an attacker to perform arbitrary file overwrite on the host system, potentially modifying critical files and compromising system integrity.

rule_message: Affected versions of h2o are vulnerable to Inefficient Regular Expression Complexity / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. The /3/Parse endpoint constructs and applies a regular expression using user-specified input, which can be manipulated to induce catastrophic backtracking. This lets an attacker send multiple concurrent requests that exhaust all available processing threads, leading to a complete denial of service in the H2O machine learning platform.

rule_message: Affected versions of golang.org/x/net are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. The HTTP/2 vulnerability occurs when a malicious client rapidly creates and resets requests, causing excessive server resource consumption. Despite the MaxConcurrentStreams setting limiting the total requests, resetting an ongoing request enables the attacker to initiate a new request concurrently.

rule_message: Affected versions of github.com/opencontainers/runc are vulnerable to Exposure Of File Descriptor To Unintended Control Sphere ('File Descriptor Leak'). The vulnerability involves container breakout through `docker build` and `docker run`, originating from the sequence of actions when applying the WORKDIR directive in the Dockerfile. This issue occurs as the specified directory is entered using chdir before closing specific privileged host directory file descriptors, allowing an attacker to exploit it by designating one of these privileged file descriptors through the `/proc/self/fd/` directory as the argument to chdir. As a result, the privileged file descriptor remains accessible even after closing during regular operations before handing off to the command defined in the Dockerfile, whether at build or runtime.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Uncontrolled Recursion / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. A malicious SavedModel can embed a GraphDef function that calls itself (direct self-recursion). TensorFlow does not validate against recursive function definitions when loading a SavedModel, so resolving each NodeDef leads to unbounded recursion, causing a stack overflow at runtime and resulting in a denial-of-service.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. A typo in TensorFlow's SpecializeType implementation causes the inner loop to call `mutable_args(i)` instead of `mutable_args(j)`, allowing heap out-of-bounds read/write of full_type arguments. An attacker who supplies a maliciously crafted model or graph with specially crafted operator full types can trigger heap corruption when the model is loaded, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or denial of service.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to  Integer Overflow or Wraparound. An integer overflow in TensorFlow's grappler cost estimator can be triggered by a maliciously crafted graph with extremely large tensor dimensions. In `OpLevelCostEstimator::CalculateTensorSize`, the product of the element count and element size (`count * size`) isn't checked for overflow, so it can wrap around and yield a much smaller (or negative) tensor size. Downstream code that allocates or indexes based on this miscomputed size may then under-allocate buffers or perform out-of-bounds accesses, leading to memory corruption.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions / Reachable Assertion. A denial-of-service crash can occur during shape inference when TensorFlow attempts to specialize an op's full_type attributes. In InferenceContext::PreInputInit it uses DCHECK to verify that full_type::SpecializeType succeeded, then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the result. Because DCHECK is a no-op in release builds, a malformed or malicious op definition whose type specialization fails will hit ValueOrDie() on an error status, crashing the process.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere / Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition. In several TensorFlow utility and library routines, Python's insecure tempfile.mktemp is used to generate temporary file (and even directory) names without atomic creation. This TOC/TOU race allows a local attacker or malicious process to pre-create or hijack the path before TensorFlow uses it, potentially leading to unintended file overwrite, data injection, or code execution.

An attacker who supplies a maliciously crafted model or graph with specially crafted operator full types can trigger heap corruption when the model is loaded, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or denial of service.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to  Integer Overflow or Wraparound. An integer overflow in TensorFlow's grappler cost estimator can be triggered by a maliciously crafted graph with extremely large tensor dimensions. In `OpLevelCostEstimator::CalculateTensorSize`, the product of the element count and element size (`count * size`) isn't checked for overflow, so it can wrap around and yield a much smaller (or negative) tensor size. Downstream code that allocates or indexes based on this miscomputed size may then under-allocate buffers or perform out-of-bounds accesses, leading to memory corruption.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Integer Overflow or Wraparound. An integer overflow in TensorFlow's Grappler cost estimator (`OpLevelCostEstimator::CalculateOutputSize`) allows an attacker to supply a tensor with excessively large or numerous dimensions so that the multiplication of `output_shape.dim()` overflows. This can lead to under-allocation of buffers during cost estimation and potentially cause memory corruption or denial-of-service when processing a crafted computation graph.

rule_message: tensorflow-gpu versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3, tensorflow-cpu versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3, and tensorflow versions before 2.5.3, version 2.7.0, >= 2.6.0 before 2.6.3 are vulnerable to Null Pointer Dereference / Access Of Uninitialized Pointer. The vulnerability in TensorFlow's code for boosted trees lacks proper validation, enabling malicious users to potentially read and write beyond the boundaries of allocated memory, leading to unauthorized access and potential denial of service (DoS) attacks through nullptr dereferencing or CHECK-failures. It is recommended to use the downstream TensorFlow Decision Forests project, instead of the unmaintained boosted trees implementation.

rule_message: tensorflow-cpu versions before 2.11.1 and tensorflow versions before 2.11.1 are vulnerable to Out-Of-Bounds Write due to mismatched integer type sizes in `ValueMap::Manager::GetValueOrCreatePlaceholder`. A bug with `tfg-translate` call to `InitMlir`. The problem happens with generic functions, as it is already handled for non-generic functions. This is because they, unlike non-generic functions, are using the "old importer".

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Improper Check for Unusual or Exceptional Conditions / Reachable Assertion. A denial-of-service crash can occur during shape inference when TensorFlow attempts to specialize an op's full_type attributes. In InferenceContext::PreInputInit it uses DCHECK to verify that full_type::SpecializeType succeeded, then unconditionally calls ValueOrDie() on the result. Because DCHECK is a no-op in release builds, a malformed or malicious op definition whose type specialization fails will hit ValueOrDie() on an error status, crashing the process.

rule_message: Affected versions of tensorflow, tensorflow-cpu, and tensorflow-gpu are vulnerable to Exposure of Resource to Wrong Sphere / Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition. In several TensorFlow utility and library routines, Python's insecure tempfile.mktemp is used to generate temporary file (and even directory) names without atomic creation. This TOC/TOU race allows a local attacker or malicious process to pre-create or hijack the path before TensorFlow uses it, potentially leading to unintended file overwrite, data injection, or code execution.
